page: The UpCloud GPU-12xCPU-128GB-1xL4 is a GPU-accelerated server instance running on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9575F processor configured with 12 shared vCPUs (12 physical cores, 1.0 thread per core) operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing a high resource density of 10.67 GB per core. Acceleration is driven by a single NVIDIA L4 GPU based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, which includes 24 GB of dedicated VRAM. No local storage is bundled with this instance, and it includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data indicates highly polarized performance characteristics. Single-core CPU performance is exceptional, with stress-ng single-core metrics and single-threaded compression/decompression tasks (such as gzip and bzip3) scoring in the top tier (top 10%). Conversely, multi-core CPU performance and PassMark CPU scores fall within the average range (middle 50%). Memory performance is robust, showing strong uncached large-block read bandwidth at 254.5 GB/sec (top 25%), while write bandwidth and cached small-block read bandwidth remain average. For AI workloads, LLM text generation using a small 135M model achieves top-tier speeds of 345.71 tokens/sec, though prompt processing for the same model is average.

The qualitative cost efficiency of this instance is defined by its specialized hardware profile. The combination of a high-capacity 128.0 GB RAM array and a 24 GB NVIDIA L4 GPU makes it a resource-dense option for memory-intensive and accelerated workloads, though the shared CPU allocation and average multi-core scaling present a tradeoff for pure parallel compute tasks. The absence of local storage requires external volume attachments, which must be factored into deployment architectures. This server is suited for lightweight LLM inference, machine learning model prototyping, memory-heavy data processing, and GPU-accelerated rendering or simulation tasks.

Built on the x86_64 architecture, this instance delivers top-tier single-core CPU performance and single-threaded compression speeds, alongside strong uncached large-block memory read bandwidth of 254.5 GB/sec. However, multi-core CPU scaling and database operations perform in the average tier. The instance lacks local storage, requiring external storage solutions. With its high memory-to-core ratio of 10.67 GB per core and dedicated Ada Lovelace GPU, this server is optimized for workloads such as small-scale LLM inference, machine learning prototyping, and GPU-accelerated data processing.
